sentences: This Fire Calorimetry Database (FCD) contains results of fire experiments conducted at the NFRL.

Certain commercial entities, equipment, or materials may be identified in this database to describe an experimental procedure or concept adequately. Such identification is not intended to imply recommendation or endorsement by the National Institute of Standards and Technology, nor is it intended to imply that the entities, materials, or equipment are necessarily the best available for the purpose.

sentences: There are multiple citations for experiments contained in this database. Each project has at least one report or journal article that describes the test methods, results and conclusions of the study. This reference should be cited when referring to experiments from a single project. The NIST Technical Note 2077 [1] should be cited when referencing the calorimetry methods or uncertainty analysis in this database. Finally, the NIST Fire Calorimetry Database [2] should be cited when using video, images, or data files or summary calculations found here.

selection.rule: every single upholstered seat or sofa, and every full-scale upholstered chair mock-up, burnt alone under the NFRL's hood, with a 1 s record; chosen from the database's listing by specimen name and description before any record was opened
selection.searched: www.nist.gov/el/fcd/experiments?k=<word> for chair, sofa, couch, loveseat, recliner, armchair, upholstered, mockup, barrier, cushion, seat, furniture, foam (2026-11-13)
leftOut: Design Fires - Residential and Office Items, Test023 (Beanbag Chair F): expanded polystyrene beads in a bag, not an upholstered seat
Room Flashover Experiments to Demonstrate the Effectiveness of Barrier Fabrics, Test_1 to Test_10: each sofa burnt in a furnished room, so the record is the room's
Dry Tree Fire Hazard, WateredTree3 and Dry_Pine_Tree: a pine tree beside an upholstered chair and a shelf, so the record is not the chair's
Transient Combustion Calorimetry, Test084 to Test086 (PatioChair): plastic chairs, not upholstered
Fire Barriers in Full-Scale Chair Mock-ups, Propane Burner Check: the burner alone

method.readings: the suite's 5 s means of the 1 s record (each the mean of the readings in (s - 2.5, s + 2.5], s = 0, 5, 10 ... s from ignition, the file's Time column), for the peak, the window and the fit; as the FSRI part
method.window: from the first 5 s mean above 25 kW (t >= 0) to the first at 90 % of the 5 s peak, both included; as the FSRI part
method.fit: least squares of q = alpha max(0, t - t0)^2, t0 free (scanned in 0.5 s steps over [window start - 1200 s, window end), refined by golden section); as the FSRI part
method.energy: the 1 s readings of the Heat Release Rate column summed from ignition to the record's end (kJ to MJ), and to the page's Fire Out event; no baseline taken off; as the FSRI part (which sums to its Suppression event)
method.mass: the page's Table 3 initial and final specimen mass (gravimetric); the effective heat of combustion is the energy over their difference
method.pageSummary: the page's Table 2 (and its hood size from Table 3), copied as published with its expanded uncertainty, for checking the reduction: the database sums from ignition to Fire Out
method.burnerChannel: the record's Burner HRR (2023 items) or NG Burner HRR (2018 mock-ups) column summed like the energy, reported beside; the 2018 mock-ups' 18 kW propane ignition burner (80 s, about 1.4 MJ) is not metered and so stays in their Heat Release Rate, which is used as it is
method.timeCheck: peakEventLessRawPeakS: the page's Peak HRR event (minutes to 0.01) less the record's raw peak time; it shows whether the record's Time column is the page's clock
